title: Default route to the internet
summary: Send everything that is not local to an upstream router with one default route, and give that router a way back.
objectives: Write a default route (0.0.0.0/0) with a next hop
See why one route replaces a route per remote network
Add the return route on the upstream router

tasks.title: Write the default route on R1
tasks.description: R1 only knows its own networks. Add a default route that sends every other destination to the ISP router at 198.51.100.2.
hints: A default route is the route to 0.0.0.0 with a prefix length of 0: it matches anything no other route matches.
Example on R1: system-view, then ip route-static 0.0.0.0 0 198.51.100.2

criteria.label: R1 has a default route via 198.51.100.2

tasks.title: Give the ISP router a way back
tasks.description: Traffic leaves, but the replies must come back. The ISP router must know where the 192.0.2.0/24 network is.
hints: The ISP router has no route to 192.0.2.0/24, so it drops the replies.

criteria.label: ISP has a route to 192.0.2.0/24 via 198.51.100.1

tasks.title: Reach the internet
tasks.description: PC1 must reach the web server and any other address behind the ISP router, using only the default route.
hints: If one address works and another does not, check that you did not write a route for a single network only.
